rateLimits.heading: Rate limits
rateLimits.intro: The API uses a three-tier rate-limit model. All limits are enforced server-side; exceeding any tier returns HTTP 429 with the headers listed below.

status.title: Public status
status.body: Service-wide observability endpoint. Always public, no per-IP or per-key bucket.

authRepo.title: Authenticated single-repo lookup
authRepo.body: Requires the X-API-Key header (find or create one from /account/keys). Limited to {limit} requests per hour per key via the durable rate_limit_buckets table. The window aligns to wall-clock hour boundaries. When the bucket is exhausted, the response is 429 with the headers below. Configurable via PUBLIC_REPO_RATE_PER_HOUR env var.

auth.title: Authenticated batch
auth.body: API-key holders are rate-limited per key by the apiKey.rateLimitPerMin field (Prisma default {limit}). Daily quota apiKey.dailyQuota (Prisma default 10000) is enforced separately. When either bucket is exhausted, the response is 429.

liveStatus.heading: Live status
liveStatus.body: Snapshot of /api/v1/status rendered on this page at request time. Click any field to open the raw JSON.

downloadSpec.heading: Download API spec
downloadSpec.body: A machine-readable summary of every public endpoint — paths, methods, auth, rate limits, cache semantics, response samples, and error codes. No OpenAPI dependency; consumers parse it as plain JSON.

howCachingWorks.heading: How caching works
howCachingWorks.intro: Every public endpoint reads through the same cache+scheduler pipeline. Once a repo is in the database, subsequent calls return from local storage without hitting GitHub.

steps.step1: Client hits an API endpoint (e.g. POST /api/query).
steps.step2: Server checks the local repository cache first. On hit, it returns immediately with the cached record.
steps.step3: On miss, the server queues a refresh job against the GitHub token pool, waits synchronously for the first response, writes the row to the database, and returns.
steps.step4: A background scheduler (default every 60s) drains the refresh queue; a nightly sweep re-enqueues every ok repo so the cache stays fresh.
steps.step5: If GitHub is unreachable, the server serves the most recent cached row with a `stale: true` flag instead of failing — better slow than down.

errorCodes.heading: Error codes
errorCodes.intro: Every 4xx/5xx response carries a machine-readable `code` alongside the human-readable `error` string. Clients should branch on `code` for retry decisions; the `error` field is for logs only.

codes.bad_request: Request body or parameters failed validation.
codes.forbidden: Credentials are valid but the caller lacks permission (e.g. inactive API key).
codes.not_found: The requested resource does not exist (e.g. GitHub returned 404 for that repo).
codes.conflict: The request conflicts with the current state of the resource.
codes.rate_limited: Rate limit exceeded. Honor the Retry-After header.
codes.internal_error: Server-side failure. Safe to retry with exponential backoff.
codes.unavailable: Service is down or a dependency is unreachable. Try again later.

development.title: Use the API, run it locally, or contribute
development.lede: Three doors into this codebase: talk to a running instance, run your own copy, or send changes back upstream.

apiUsers.heading: 1 · Using the public API
apiUsers.body: Every public endpoint returns JSON and is documented below. Rate limits apply per API key (authenticated) or per IP (anonymous). All times are ISO 8601 UTC.
apiUsers.quickCheckBody: No authentication required. Should always return 200 with ok: true if the service is up.
apiUsers.singleRepoBody: Same endpoint used by the public repo detail page. Falls through to GitHub on cache miss and enqueues a background refresh.
apiUsers.v1StatusBody: system health snapshot (DB, token pool, queue, repo count, version)
apiUsers.v1ReposBody: one repo's cached record (cache miss → GitHub → 202 pending)
apiUsers.v1QueryBody: authenticated batch lookup up to 50 nodes per call (API key required)
apiUsers.machineReadableBody: download /api-docs.json — every public endpoint summarized as JSON (path, method, auth, rate limit, cache semantics, response example, error codes). Consumer-side parsers don't need OpenAPI.

localDev.heading: 2 · Running it locally
localDev.body: Prereqs: Node 20+, MySQL 5.7+, Git. The whole stack runs in one Node process — no Docker required.
localDev.lint: ESLint — 0 errors required (warnings OK if pre-existing)
localDev.tokenHelp: Need a GitHub token to query real repos? See the next section.

contributing.heading: 3 · Contributing changes
contributing.body: Small, focused pull requests are easiest to review. Each milestone ships as its own commit on master with a one-line summary.
contributing.forkStep3: Make your change. Follow the conventions in CLAUDE.md (TypeScript strict, server actions in src/app/_actions/, i18n keys in both messages/en.json and messages/zh.json).
contributing.forkStep4: Run the quality gates locally: npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm test
contributing.forkStep5: Open a PR against master at:
contributing.subject: Imperative subject
contributing.subjectBody: ≤72 chars, no trailing period, lower-case after the colon
contributing.bodyBody: explain WHY, not WHAT (the diff shows what). Wrap at 72 cols. Reference the milestone number if applicable.
contributing.coAuthoredBody: if you used Claude or another AI to draft the change — keep it transparent
contributing.style1: Server actions live in src/app/_actions/ with 'use server' at the top
contributing.style2: Per-user preferences mirror the lang/theme/timezone triad (cookie + DB + server action + switcher)
contributing.style3: Never use d.toISOString().slice(...) for user-facing dates — use formatDate/formatDateTime/formatTime from @/lib/format/datetime
contributing.style4: next-intl t.rich callbacks must accept the chunk argument or you'll ship "function transformed" to production
contributing.style5: DB-direct GitHub token storage (M21) — never re-introduce GITHUB_TOKENS env vars
contributing.tokenHeading: Adding a GitHub PAT for testing
contributing.tokenBody: Do NOT commit tokens. For local testing, go to /admin/github-tokens after first login and paste a PAT there — M21 stores it in the database and the pool picks it up immediately. For production, rotate on GitHub after every leak rather than trying to scrub it from old backups.

meta.title: Deployment & operations · GitHub Metadata Cache
meta.description: Production deployment guide: env vars, first boot, SMTP, GitHub tokens, hardening, rollouts, monitoring.

deployment.heading: Deployment & operations
deployment.lede: Everything you need to take githubcache from a fresh checkout to a production instance behind a reverse proxy. Pair this with /docs/development for local-run details.

prereq.heading: Prerequisites
prereq.mysql: MySQL 5.7+ (or 8.x). The default DATABASE_URL is local; override for managed instances.
prereq.reverseProxy: A reverse proxy in front (Caddy / nginx) for HTTPS termination. The Node server itself is plain HTTP on PORT (default 5002).
prereq.smtp: An SMTP relay for invite + key approval + welcome emails. The service does NOT send mail in dev if SMTP is unconfigured.

env.heading: Environment variables
env.intro: All knobs are env vars; there is no admin UI for changing the runtime config. The minimum required are DATABASE_URL and SESSION_SECRET.

notes.sessionSecret: Random ≥32 chars. Rotating it logs out every active session — never reuse across environments.
notes.port: The custom server (Next + scheduler + pool) listens on this port. Default 5002 to match the local dev scripts.
notes.nodeEnv: `production` enables Next.js prod build + drops stack traces from /api errors. Always set to `production` in deploy.
notes.logLevel: pino level. `info` for prod, `debug` for local.
notes.schedulerTick: How often the refresh worker checks for jobs. 1s in dev, 60s in prod. Lowering it to 1s in prod risks hot loops.
notes.schedulerBatch: Max jobs claimed per tick. Default 5; raise if GitHub rate budget allows.
notes.publicLookup: DEPRECATED — kept for env-var back-compat. /api/v1/repos is now per-key.
notes.publicRepo: Per-API-key hourly ceiling for /api/v1/repos. Default 50 000 (≈14 req/sec sustained).
notes.signupRate: Per-IP hourly ceiling for /signup. Default 50 000; tighten if the instance is exposed to the open internet.
notes.gitCommit: Surfaces in /api/v1/status. CI should set this from `$GITHUB_SHA` so operators can confirm the deployed build.

firstBoot.heading: First boot
firstBoot.install: install production dependencies only (no devDependencies in the image).
firstBoot.migrate: apply schema migrations without prompts. Run before the app first starts serving.
firstBoot.build: compile the Next.js app for prod (faster cold start, smaller images).
firstBoot.start: launch the custom server. The scheduler + GitHub token pool initialize here; check stdout for `listening on port N`.
firstBoot.note: Run migrations as a separate step (not inside the app's startup) so a crashed migration doesn't take down a healthy instance.

smtp.heading: SMTP setup (admin UI at /admin/email)
smtp.intro: The service uses one SMTP credential for all transactional mail (invite, password reset, signup welcome, key approval, key request). Without it, signup + key approval flows run but the user never gets the email.
smtp.step2: Enter host / port / user / password / from address. Use STARTTLS on 587 or SMTPS on 465 — the form toggles TLS.
smtp.step3: Click "Send test" to confirm the relay accepts mail. Save only after the test arrives.

tokens.heading: GitHub tokens (admin UI at /admin/github-tokens)
tokens.intro: Add at least 2 tokens so the pool can rotate when one hits its 5000 req/hr cap. All values are stored in the github_tokens table (M21) — no env-var config required.
tokens.step1: Generate a fine-scoped PAT in GitHub → Settings → Developer settings → Personal access tokens. Use the `public_repo` scope (or `repo` if you'll cache private repos).
tokens.step2: In /admin/github-tokens, paste the token, add a label, save. The pool picks it up immediately — no restart.
tokens.step3: Add a second token so the pool has redundancy. The /api/v1/status endpoint shows the active + exhausted + total counts.

prod.heading: Production hardening
prod.processManager: Run under systemd / pm2 / a k8s pod. The server traps SIGTERM and exits cleanly after scheduler drains.
prod.reverseProxy: Caddy or nginx in front. Force HTTPS; the Node process serves plain HTTP only.
prod.https: Required — the X-API-Key header must not travel over cleartext. Caddy auto-issues Let's Encrypt certs.
prod.logs: Pipe stdout to your log aggregator (CloudWatch, Loki, Datadog). Pino emits structured JSON in prod.
prod.backups: MySQL logical backups via mysqldump (M17 ships the `Backup now` button at /admin/database). Keep ≥7 days of daily backups.
prod.scaling: Single-process today. The Prisma pool is bumped to 32 (src/lib/db/client.ts) so 100-concurrent tests pass. For higher concurrency, run multiple instances behind a shared MySQL.

rollout.heading: Rollouts & rollbacks
rollout.intro: githubcache uses forward-only Prisma migrations. A bad migration can't be auto-rolled-back — rehearse in staging.
rollout.step1: Build a new image. Set GIT_COMMIT to the new SHA.
rollout.step2: Run `npx prisma migrate deploy` against the production DB BEFORE starting new app instances.
rollout.step3: Restart app instances one at a time (rolling restart). Health-check via GET /api/v1/status between restarts.
rollout.rollback: Rollback = redeploy the previous image. The DB is forward-only; if a migration is destructive, write a follow-up migration that restores the schema.

monitor.heading: Monitoring
monitor.intro: Five surfaces cover most of what you need:
monitor.publicStatusBody: public dashboard — DB, scheduler, tokens, queue, repo cache. Update the page to refresh.
monitor.auditBody: every privileged action: login, key approval, user disable, etc. Filter by actor / target / date.
monitor.queriesBody: recent API traffic with cache hit/miss + status code. Useful for spotting abusive keys or upstream GitHub issues.

api-v1-status.summary: System status — DB, token pool, queue, repository counts, version.
api-v1-status.description: Read-only observability endpoint. Always public, no rate limit. Returns 503 when the DB is down so load balancers can take the instance out of rotation.

api-v1-repos.summary: Fetch a single repository metadata record from the cache.
api-v1-repos.description: Authenticated read of the cache for a single repo. Returns the same shape as the repo detail page at /repo/[owner]/[name]. If the cache is empty, falls through to a fresh GitHub fetch. M26.x: now requires the X-API-Key header (was anonymous per-IP before).
api-v1-repos.auth: Requires the X-API-Key header with an active API key.

errors.403-invalid_api_key: Key not found, revoked, or attached to a disabled account.
errors.404-not_found: fetch_status=not_found (GitHub returned 404 or owner/name is invalid).
errors.503-service_unavailable: fetch_status=error or no GitHub tokens configured.

api-query.summary: Batch-fetch up to 50 repositories with a single API key.
api-query.description: Authenticated batch endpoint for API key holders. Returns results in the same order as the input nodes; partial failures are reported per-node via the discriminated union.
api-query.rateLimit: rateLimitPerMin (per API key, default 60) durable bucket

request.nodes-description: Up to 50 repo refs to fetch.

headers.Retry-After-description: Seconds until the rate limit resets.

errors.403-invalid_api_key: Key not found or status != active.

getStarted.title: From sign-up to your first API call in 4 steps
getStarted.lede: githubcache is a cache for GitHub repository metadata. Self-signup is open — you create your own account, request a key, and an admin reviews it. This page walks you through the whole path.

meta.title: Quickstart · GitHub Metadata Cache
meta.description: Sign up, request an API key, get approved, and make your first call in four steps.

step1.heading: Create an account at /signup
step1.body: Open /signup, enter an email + password (≥8 chars) and an optional display name. The account is created immediately — no email verification, no waiting on an admin. You land in /account as a signed-in operator.
step1.action2: Fill in email, password, optional display name.
step1.action3: Submit. You're auto-logged-in and redirected to /account.

step2.heading: Request an API key from /account/keys/request
step2.body: From your account dashboard, open the API keys page and click "Request a new key". Give the key a short name (e.g. `ci-pipeline`) and an optional description of what you'll use it for. The request is created with status `pending` and a self-requested prefix (`ghc_usr_…`) so admins can spot user-initiated requests at a glance.
step2.action1: In /account, click "Request a new API key".
step2.action2: Enter a name + optional description and submit.
step2.action3: The new key appears in your list with status `pending`.

step3.heading: Wait for an admin to approve
step3.body: An admin receives a `key-requested` email (subject: `<your-email> requested an API key on <site>`) with a deep link straight to /admin/api-keys/[id]. They open the key detail page, click Approve, and the system generates the plaintext token.
step3.calloutBody: The plaintext token is shown ONCE — copy it the moment it appears. githubcache cannot recover it later. If SMTP is configured, the same token is also emailed to you.

step4.heading: Make your first call
step4.body: All three calls require your `X-API-Key` header. The status endpoint is the only exception — it's a public health check. Copy and paste; replace `YOUR_KEY_HERE` with the token from step 3.
step4.example1Body: Status endpoint confirms the service is up and reports cache stats. No auth required.
step4.example2Body: Authenticated read of the cache for a single repo. Send your key as the `X-API-Key` header. Cache miss queues a refresh and waits synchronously. Rate limit: 50 000 / hour / key.
step4.example3Body: Authenticated batch lookup. Send your key as the `X-API-Key` header; pass up to 50 owner/name pairs in the body.

errors.forbidden: Key invalid, revoked, or your account is disabled.
errors.rate_limited: Per-key or per-IP bucket exhausted — wait `Retry-After` seconds.
errors.not_found: Repository doesn't exist on GitHub (or is private).
